title: How video latents work, and each model's frame grid
hook: Ask three models for 120 frames and get 113, 117 and 124. Why, and how to ask so you get what you typed.

verified.claim: LTX floors to 8k + 1 frames, with 128 channels at one thirty-second of the width and height.
Wan 2.2 5B floors to 4k + 1 frames, with 48 channels at one sixteenth.
H3 rounds up to 17k + 5 frames, with 24 channels at one sixteenth, and its latent frames cover 1, 4, 4, 4, 4 frames in turn.
The lab's H3 port matches the real temporal_shape for 100, 124 and 736 frames.
Frame counts of the gallery clips were read with ffprobe: LTX 145 and 121, Wan 121, H3 124.
nm_video validates and runs on a CPU.

unchecked: The token counts assume one token per latent position for LTX and a 2 x 2 patch for Wan and H3. We read those in the model code, but did not run a model to count them.
We did not measure quality. Nothing here says that any grid gives better motion than another.
